title: Gradient steps down a loss curve
prompts: The yellow curve is the loss L(w) = (curvature/2)(w − 2)² + 0.5. Each dashed blue caret (^) above it marks where the weight sits after another step w ← w − η·L′(w); the first caret sits at the starting weight w₀.
With η = 0.3, watch the carets bunch up as they approach w = 2: the slope shrinks near the bottom, so the steps shrink too, even though η never changes.
Set η = 1 with curvature 1. One step lands exactly on the minimum. Why? Here η × curvature = 1, so the update cancels the whole error w − 2 at once.
Push η past 1 (try 1.6). The carets jump back and forth across the valley: overshooting, but still converging because |1 − η·curvature| < 1.
Now try η = 2.2. Each step overshoots by more than it corrects, so the carets march outward and leave the plot. Divergence starts exactly at η = 2 / curvature.
Keep η = 0.8 and raise the curvature to 3. A learning rate that was safe on a gentle valley now diverges on a steep one. That is why learning rates are tuned per problem.

Hover the plot: f(x) is the loss and compare shows a value only at visited weights. Move the starting weight w₀ to the right of 2 and the steps come from the other side, because the slope changes sign.
